title.value: More Than Meets the Eye: Art Engages the Social Brain
title.justification: The title accurately captures the central theme of the paper, which is the exploration of how art interacts with and engages the neural mechanisms related to social cognition.
title.quote:
van Leeuwen JEP, Boomgaard J, Bzdok D, Crutch SJ and Warren JD
(2022) More Than Meets the Eye: Art Engages the Social Brain.

extractions.description: This paper discusses how art engages the social brain by mapping art processing onto the social brain connectome. It posits that art involves complex neural dynamics similar to those used in social cognition, and suggests potential applications in mental health and dementia care. The paper promotes interdisciplinary research between neuroaesthetics and art professionals.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper mainly focuses on the relationship between art and the social brain, exploring neural dynamics and potential implications for mental health and neurological conditions, rather than addressing ecological or climate-related themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Complementary to the unquestionable value of art for art’s sake, we argue that its neural grounding in the social brain raises important practical implications for mental health, and the care of people living with dementia and other neurological conditions.

primary_category.justification: The central theme of the paper is not related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development; it is more about the relationship between art and neural processes, particularly in social cognition.
primary_category.quote: The strong overlap between the neural dynamics of art processing and social cognition in the artistic brain connectome raises clinical implications that may suggest practical diagnostic and therapeutic applications.

secondary_categories.justification: Since the primary category is 'N/A' and the theme does not directly relate to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, there are no secondary categories applicable in this context.
secondary_categories.quote: This recent paradigm shift in social neuroscience promises to have an equally transformative impact on neuroaesthetics, and our view of art as an construct of the human social brain.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not align with any specific Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development sub-categories, focusing instead on the neural and social implications of art.
primary_sub_category.quote: We present a prima facie case for visual art as a social brain phenomenon, drawing pre-eminently on evidence derived from the social brain connectome to propose an “artistic brain connectome.”

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Due to the lack of relevance to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, secondary sub-categories are not applicable.
secondary_sub_categories.quote:
These findings are congruent
with the functional profiles of AI, aMCC, SMA and IFG in
the social brain connectome, which implicate these regions in
a range of cognitive functions related to action execution and
inhibition.

applications.value: Art therapy and mental health support
applications.justification: The paper suggests practical applications of the artistic brain connectome for mental health and dementia care, providing insights into how art can be used for therapeutic purposes.
applications.quote: Complementary to the unquestionable value of art for art’s sake, we argue that its neural grounding in the social brain raises important practical implications for mental health, and the care of people living with dementia and other neurological conditions.

new_primary_category.justification: Given the focus on the intersection of art and social brain functions, a new category of 'Neuroaesthetics' which studies these relationships in the context of brain science could be relevant.
new_primary_category.quote: We hope that our framework will be of use in contemporary art practice and education as well as neuroscientific research and ultimately clinical practice.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category could be focused on understanding how the brain's neural networks engage with and process art, reflecting the paper's emphasis on mapping these processes.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We present a prima facie case for visual art as a social brain phenomenon, drawing pre-eminently on evidence derived from the social brain connectome to propose an “artistic brain connectome.”
